reader.requirement: An out-of-line PERFORM procedure-name-1 THRU procedure-name-2 starts at procedure-name-1 and returns when execution completes procedure-name-2, whatever path reaches it: GO TO and PERFORM statements may occur inside the range (including GO TO out of the span and back, an inverted range whose procedure-name-2 precedes procedure-name-1, sections and paragraphs mixed, pn1 = pn2), and an EXIT paragraph may serve as the common return point of several paths.

edition-consulted.switches: construct SegmentNumbersRemoved2002: at 85 the PERFORM range's reached segments are checked against §1985:XVI.3.3.2; absent from 2002 (a separate rule, not GR8's execution)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition.Edition|Year|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry|CobolVersion in ControlFlowBinder.cs, DispatchEmitter.cs and PcRange.cs: the only hit on the PERFORM path is Segmentation.CheckProcedures; the range composition and the dispatcher's return-at-end-of-procedure-name-2 are edition-invariant.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the four witnesses cover the inverted range, an EXIT common endpoint, range composition and a SORT procedure range; a GO TO leaving the span and re-entering at procedure-name-2, a section-THRU-section range and PERFORM THRU with TIMES over a nested PERFORM sharing the endpoint are covered only by pf1.

reader.notes: BindPerform composes the range as procedure-name-1's start through procedure-name-2's end (PcRange.Through) and the dispatcher returns when the exit procedure completes wherever it lies, so the inverted and GO TO-threaded ranges behave as GR8 says. Classes a, d and f do not apply to a control-flow rule; class b was read here as the degenerate and multi-path forms the rule permits.
